title: Stale file_path metadata
body:
I moved some folders, and while the preview images refreshed, the file_path in the metadata.json files did not, so none of those loras can be loaded in the LoraManager Lora Loader anymore. Can you either deduce the file_path each time or update it on refresh? Thanks!

author: broken

comments.body: Thanks for the feedback! When you say "moved some folders," do you mean you manually moved them in the file explorer?
Yes. That's what I mean.

I wouldn't recommend manually moving folders at this time. The watchdog monitors additions and deletions within loras_root, but when files are moved manually, it only detects new additions—not deletions. Plus due to the unpredictable order of multiple file moves (e.g., the LoRA file moving before its metadata file), cache inconsistencies or even metadata loss may occur.

If I have time, I’ll look into a more sophisticated solution to handle this better. For now, I recommend using the bulk operation feature in LoRA Manager to move files within the interface safely.

That said, I've submitted a fix that will attempt to correct incorrect file paths when rebuilding the cache on startup. If you're experiencing issues where metadata errors prevent LoRAs from loading, please try restarting ComfyUI and see if that resolves the problem.

Also, LoRA Stack is already supported in v0.7.36, and checkpoint management is planned for a future update.

Yeah, I noticed that behavior with the monitor.

I'm away atm, but will test this change and the lora stacks when I get back home in a few days. Thanks!
Confirming this was fixed. Thanks!

title: HI,bro.Are you considering increasing the management of the checkpoint model?
body: HI,bro.Are you considering increasing the management of the checkpoint model?
author: DreamLoveBetty

comments.body:
Hi. Thanks for checking out my project! Increasing the management of checkpoint models is a great idea, but there are a few things I need to consider:

1. I'm not sure if the demand for managing checkpoints is as high as for managing LoRAs, since checkpoints are generally fewer in number, and many users (including myself) only use one or a few checkpoints. In contrast, LoRAs are much more numerous and are often combined in different ways.
2. Supporting checkpoint models would involve a significant amount of additional work, primarily due to the need to refactor the current codebase.

Considering all of this, while I might consider adding checkpoint management in the future, it's unlikely to be a priority in the near term.

Hello and thanks for your reply. It is true that the management of checkpoint models is not very urgent, but now there are more and more third-party fine-tuning or merging models based on several models in the community, such as: (SDXL/pony/iLL/anime), plus flux, etc., as you said, you can consider adding them in the future. Well, thanks for your work!

title: 3 suggestions: Implement Fuzzy search + add suggested strength pulled from Civitai + add a toggle for deep search
body:
1- I noticed that the current implementation of the search function, if I search for my model  "Fares Fares - Flux.1 D" using "fares flux", I don't find it. I think fuzzy search could be a perfect addition to the project, since it also helps search words misspelled etc.

2- You have the trigger word highlighted to copy, which is great! I also think the suggested strength is a very important parameter that I could not find in the models card. Not everyone fill it on Civitai, but some people do. My previously mentioned model for example works better at 1.37 strength.

3- If I click on a folder let's say (lora/Flux), it only searches within that main folder but doesn't include the subfolders like (lora/Flux/characters). It would be great if you could implement a recursive "deep" search toggle to be activated or not in these cases, to ensure that files in all subfolders are also searched. A toggle would be better because sometimes you might want to exclude subfolder, and sometimes you want to see everything.

Thanks very much! I'm loving this extension!
author: diodiogod

comments.body:
Thank you for your great suggestions! I’m glad to hear that you're enjoying the extension.

1. Regarding the search function, I’ll definitely consider adding fuzzy search in the next update.

2. As for the suggested strength, unfortunately, the CivitAI API doesn’t currently return this data, even if the Lora author has specified it during model submission or mentioned it in the description. Implementing this feature will require some additional work, as I'll need time to evaluate and test potential solutions. I’ll look into this and aim to come up with a balanced approach.

3. For the folder search, I agree that adding a recursive "deep" search toggle would be a useful feature. This will allow for searching through subfolders when needed, while also providing the flexibility to exclude them when desired. I’ll consider adding this in a future update as well.
